subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should OpenClaw add recurring native PowerShell smoke coverage for `check:docs`, `build:strict-smoke`, or a narrower proven command set in the existing Windows CI lane?
rationale: The direction fits the test-infrastructure roadmap, but it changes recurring Windows runner work and the active PR shows one proposed command is not yet safe in that lane.

options.title: Land after full proof
options.body: Accept the smoke lane only after the chosen commands pass in Windows `pwsh` and the PR includes redacted successful proof for the exact command set.

options.title: Start narrower
options.body: Land only the native PowerShell commands that already pass and leave `build:strict-smoke` or heavier coverage to a follow-up.

options.title: Defer CI scope
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause the recurring Windows smoke lane until runner budget or release priorities justify it.

recommendation.title: Land after full proof
recommendation.body: Accept the smoke lane only after the chosen commands pass in Windows `pwsh` and the PR includes redacted successful proof for the exact command set.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent overlap across CI workflow stabilization and the PowerShell-safe docs tooling that the smoke lane would exercise.
